# Matt Waldman's RSP Cast — 2024-02-19

**Raw transcript:** `raw/ingested/rsp-cast/2024-02-19-rsp-feel-it-or-fk-it-never-too-early-to-draft-edition-rsp-cast-with-bob-ha.md` (immutable — do not edit)

## Summary

*Feel It Or F@#k It* with **Bob Harris** (co-host, not a tracked expert). The
first episode of the year's redraft cycle proper — both hosts are already
deep in early best-ball mocks a full week after the Super Bowl, and frame the
whole episode as reps: figuring out 2024 values and landing-spot bets months
before free agency and the draft actually happen, then adjusting as real
information arrives. Dense with veteran free-agent and pending-free-agent
market calls plus a first real round of 2024 quarterback-prospect
"feel it or f\*\*k it" verdicts.

**Free-agent running backs.** [[Derrick Henry]] gets the episode's clearest
value call — currently a fifth-round redraft price Waldman calls a likely
"huge steal" given he'd have considered him in the third round on talent,
with Baltimore, the Chargers, Dallas and Philadelphia floated as landing
spots. [[Josh Jacobs]] is grouped with Henry as the other back Waldman is
confident lands a real starting job somewhere. New page [[Joe Mixon]] gets a
detailed Dallas-fit case built around what [[Tony Pollard]]'s pre-2023 hype
promised but hasn't delivered. New page [[Alvin Kamara]] is flagged as cap-
squeeze uncertain in New Orleans but a real weeks-4-17 top-4 fantasy back if
he stays, especially under new Shanahan-tree OC Klint Kubiak.

**Free-agent/situational receivers and QBs.** [[Stefon Diggs]] gets Waldman's
fullest "blip on the radar, not a cliff" defense yet — a scheme/role read
(Buffalo's pecking order, not decline) with a projected fall to the [[Tyler Lockett]]
range. [[Keenan Allen]] is "irresistible" at a fourth-round price
if the Chargers keep him, tied directly to a detailed [[Justin Herbert]]
(new page) scheme-history case for new OC Greg Roman/HC Jim Harbaugh not
being the receiving-corps-killer their run-heavy reputation suggests. New
pages [[Derek Carr]] (a specific Trevor Penning-protection mechanism behind a
rough start/strong finish) and [[Justin Fields]] (Atlanta or Pittsburgh as
his best outcomes) get full evaluations. New page [[Rashid Shaheed]] gets a
bounded WR3/4 grade. [[Tua Tagovailoa]] gets a more optimistic redraft read
than [[Matt Harmon]]'s recent critical one, framed around the same
"underrated limited thrower" archetype as [[Kirk Cousins]]/[[Jared Goff]]. A
three-way [[Russell Wilson]]/[[Jerry Jeudy]]/[[Courtland Sutton]] discussion
(all new pages) relays a harder-line outside take from **Dwain McFarland**
(not a tracked expert) that Cover-2-high defenses ended Wilson's viability,
which Waldman only partly buys, pointing instead at a weak Denver receiver
room.

**Tampa Bay chain reaction.** [[Baker Mayfield]]'s "totally feeling it" 2024
outlook is now explicitly conditioned on [[Mike Evans]] (reportedly nearing
free agency after a missed contract deadline) and [[Chris Godwin]] staying,
with new OC Liam Coen (a prior Mayfield-approved Rams assistant) replacing
Dave Canales.

**2024 QB prospect verdicts.** First real round of grades on the top of the
class: [[Caleb Williams]] gets an explicit "not all three" (with [[Drake Maye]]
and [[Jayden Daniels]]) verdict on hitting their draft capital, with
Williams "most likely" the one who does, alongside a Jay Cutler/Jeff George
bust comp. Daniels and Maye both get bench-year prescriptions for different
processing reasons. [[Bo Nix]] gets a harder "bubble screen Bo" framing
relayed from outside evaluator **Dan Hatman** (not a tracked expert, cited
from a private conversation). [[Michael Penix Jr.]] gets upgraded back to
Waldman's top outlier-QB pick, alongside a Ryan-Grubb-to-Seattle landing-spot
note. [[J.J. McCarthy]] and [[Jack Plummer]] get shorter status-update
bullets.

**Other.** [[George Pickens]] gets a coachability case study tied to Mike
Tomlin's organizational patience (see [[Player Development and Coachability]]).

## Not given pages

Zach Moss (a single free-agent ADP-value mention, no evaluative content),
Michael Pratt (Tulane prospect — "needs a bit more time, nice pocket guy," a
passing deep-league mention), Skylar Thompson (deep-league roster mention
only), Trevor Penning, Michael Thomas and Chris Olave (New Orleans context
for the [[Derek Carr]] read, not standalone evaluations), Sam Howell (cited
only as a development-runway comp for [[Bo Nix]]), Deshaun Watson (named only
as a hypothetical player Cleveland would move on from). Drake London, Kyle
Pitts and Bijan Robinson are referenced only as Atlanta's existing weapons in
the [[Justin Fields]] discussion — no new evaluative content beyond what's
already on their pages. [[Desmond Ridder]] is referenced only as a processing-
speed baseline for Fields — no update to his own page. Jim Harbaugh, Greg
Roman, Cliff Kingsbury, Mike Tomlin, Bill Belichick, Raheem Morris, Ryan
Grubb, Liam Coen, Jeff Brohm and Klint Kubiak (coaches — out of scope).
